newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed lower in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Thursday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.48/98.53 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.53/98.58, September 2001 at S$97.29/97.34 against S$97.39/97.44 and June 2003 at S$95.29/95.34 from S$95.39/95.44.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/8 3 percent against Wednesday's 2-1/2 2-3/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.65/1.65 percent from Wednesday's yield of 1.40/1.35 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.97/1.92 percent versus 1.88/1.83 percent.
